The Constitutional Court in Crisis

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Is a lack of leadership causing instability in the highest court in the land

Unique Selling Point:
The Constitutional Court is the highest court in South Africa. As such it is the protector and custodian of South Africa's constitution and as such, democracy.

With Chief Justice Moegeng Moegeng's tenure coming to an end in October and a host of other vacancies due to the retirement of several justices, this is a court in transition.

This coincides with a time in which the court itself is under attack from all sides.

We ask the question: is this a court in crisis?

Summary:
Critics argue that The Constitutional Court is in crisis, devoid of leadership and divisions on the bench leading to the Court's unraveling.

The leadership vacuum is causing instability within one of the cornerstones of democracy in South Africa. At the end of October, depending on whether the existing vacancies on the Constitutional Court are filled, only six of the Court's 11 judges will be permanent appointees. At present, there are two vacancies occasioned by the retirement of Justices Edwin Cameron and Johan Froneman. In the next month, two more vacancies will arise from the retirement of Justices Sisi Khampepe and Chris Jafta. These developments mark the most significant change to the Court's membership since 2009. Unfortunately, they also coincide with something of a leadership crisis that has befallen the Court.

From the leadership point of view, whoever will be the next Chief Justice must treat this as a serious existential problem that must be attended to without delay to avoid the judiciary descending into disrepute and chaos.

Press Release:


Constitutional Court on the Edge
At the vanguard of South Africa’s democracy as defender of a hard-won fundamental human rights, the Constitutional Court has long fulfilled its mandate to check the abuse of power by branches of government and enforce the rule of law. But more recent judgments have signalled a court deeply divided and at odds over politically sensitive cases. Could an increasingly politicised caseload and a leadership vacuum at the helm hasten the court’s unravelling and undermine the leadership role the country’s future depends on?
Producer: Julian Sun | Presenter: Bongani Bingwa

Script:


OPENING LINK: This is the Constitutional Court, the highest court in the land. It is charged with protecting South Africa’s constitution. But now in the face of intense criticism about its leadership. Does the apex court find itself at a crossroads?

V/O: In an era of state capture and rampant corruption, the Constitutional Court remains a beacon of hope for many. Time and time again it has reaffirmed the rule of law.

But sustained attacks have cast doubt on its integrity, causing many to fear for the future of one of South Africa’s most revered institutions. Mbekezeli Benjamin is a researcher for Judges Matter


· Mbekezeli on leadership crisis at the Court

V/O: Lawson Naidoo is the executive secretary of the Council for the Advancement of the South African Constitution (or CASAC). He believes the court is in crisis

BEATS:
· Lawson, you co-authored an article in which you say that the Constitutional Court is in crisis. Why do you believe that?
LINK: The Chief Justice is the head of the judiciary and this is the seat he occupies at the Constitutional Court. For the past 10 years that man has been Moegeng Moegeng and as his term of office draws to a close, the choice for his replacement is seen by many as one of the most consequential decisions for our judiciary

V/O: Judge Moegeng Moegeng exits the court as the only Chief Justice to have served his full term.

How will he be remembered? Karyn Maughan is a legal Journalist for News24

· He came in with controversy, he led well in the middle, he ended in controversy
V/O: He led the court through turbulent times, winning respect for the unanimous Nkandla judgment that found that then-President Jacob Zuma broke his oath to uphold the constitution.

· Karyn on the wheels coming off

V/O: He was found to have violated the code of judicial conduct for statements he made regarding Israel and ordered to apologize.
He has appealed the finding citing his religious beliefs.
· Karyn on vaccines
V/O: Judge Moegeng’s tenure effectively ended in May, meaning he was not present for the Constitutional Court’s most controversial decision this year - to send former President Jacob Zuma to prison for contempt of court.

While judicial dissent is not unusual, did the 7-2 majority decision reveal discord between the justices?

BEATS
· There was dissent on the bench from Justices Chris Jafta and Leona Theron – which was the basis for President Zuma’s recission application. Tell me about that.
V/O: The apparent animosity between the justices surrounding the Zuma judgment is a far cry from the collegial atmosphere Judge Albie Sachs recalls from his time at the court.

· Albie Sachs on making decisions collectively and encouraging dissent.

V/O President Cyril Ramaphosa is tasked with appointing the new Chief Justice and that process is already underway. For the first time, a public call for nominations has been allowed.
· Karyn talks about the process of selecting the next chief justice
· Mbekezele on the why this is so important
V/O: But on that list are Western Cape Judge President John Hlope – who was found guilty for gross judicial misconduct, as well as Public Protector Busisiwe Mkwebane who is also facing impeachment
· Karyn on John Hlope and Busisiwe Mkwebane
· Identify the favourites to be the next chief justice

LINK: The 11 justices who sit on this court are the ultimate defenders of our democracy. With several of them retiring, among them the Chief Justice himself, this is a court in transition

V/O: Apart from the seat vacated by the Chief Justice, 4 other judges have recently retired resulting in 5 vacancies on the bench.

The Judicial Service Commission is the body that recommends candidates for appointment to the President.

It is made up of representatives from the legal community, the executive and MP’s including the opposition.

· Comments from Mbekezeli on the vacancies on the court

V/O: Interviews to fill vacancies on the Constitutional Court were first held in April but were so contentious they were challenged by CASAC for being unconstitutional.

· Lawson on why they challenged the process.

V/O: The Hearings were re-run last week with more decorum. However, the same 5 candidates selected in April were again shortlisted in October, raising eyebrows. Legal Journalist Erin Bates covered the proceedings.

· Get comments from Erin, & Karyn on the new hearings

V/O: The JSC has been accused of becoming too politicized. Could that be why two highly qualified candidates Judge David Unterhalter and Advocate Alan Dodson were overlooked?


· We bring in the fact that neither white candidates made the shortlist


V/O: With the apex court in transition and questions over the objectivity of the JSC, is the Judiciary in crisis?

· Karyn warns that the court is in crisis

BONGANI: So what type of court will he be inheriting?

· End comment from Erin about the stakes.










TEASER:

PROMO 1 (21”) This is the Constitutional Court, the highest court in the land. Since its inception, the court has shown itself to be worthy custodians and protectors of South Africa’s hard-earned democracy. But now with a changing of the guard and the choosing of a new Chief Justice, what will its future hold?

Promo 2 (21”): Leaderless and with 5 vacancies on the bench, the Constitutional Court finds itself at a crossroads.

Karyn Maughn: I think its manifestly apparent that the judiciary is a state of profound crisis

Will the choosing a new Chief Justice stabilise the court and steer it in a new direction?

Studio Promo (11”): With 5 vacancies on the Constitutional Court, the appointment of a new Chief Justice is seen by many as crucial for its future. We unpack the challenges facing the highest court in the land.
